Inquam Photos/Octav Ganea via REUTERS The X account of Andrew Tate, the MAGA-aligned influencer facing extradition for a slew of charges that include child pornography, bemoaned conditions in his jail cell Sunday – and was immediately mocked. Tate, who’s frequently boasted about his closeness to the Trump family, appeared to be communicating from a Special Housing Unit following his arrest in Florida earlier this month. “My water faucet is broken” the post states. "I am not allowed bottles of water in SHU. I have nothing clean to drink." Both Tate and his brother Tristan face extradition to the United Kingdom for charges that include rape and sex trafficking, reports show. Their attorney has denied the charges and declared his clients innocent. The Tate brothers were previously arrested in 2022 on rape and human trafficking charges in Romania, though the case stalled following pressure from the Trump administration. "My only water comes from the shower, warm and from a brown and filthy faucet," Tate's account posted Sunday. "It has given me persistent stomach problems." A number of critics passed on extending Tate their sympathies. “Have you tried crying about it?” asked Travis Akers, a retired U.S. Navy intelligence officer and veterans advocate, in a social media post on X Sunday. Former Rep. Adam Kinzinger (R-IL) sarcastically quipped “poor guy,” while also arguing that Tate – dubbed the “king of toxic masculinity” by fans – exposed himself after his “Scooby Doo mask was ripped off,” revealing “a trembling scared beta cuck.” “This is supposed to be a manly man,” wrote Joshua Carr, a conservative political commentator and podcaster. And the “Socialist Voice” X account, formerly run by British Labour activist Scott Nelson, issued Tate some sarcastic advice for his bottled water-related challenges. “Outrageous!” reads the post on X. “You should leave a bad review on TripAdvisor. http://www.heraldglobe.com/news/27931460.text: Trump hails major progress on setting up US Army base in Poland RT.com 18 Sep 2026, 09:11 GMT+10 The president made the announcement as Russia warned European NATO members against provoking a war with Moscow The US has made major progress in negotiations to establish a military base in Poland, President Donald Trump has announced. His remarks came as Russia warned that it would retaliate if the territory of Poland or the Baltic states were used for a NATO attack against the country. Poland, which borders Russia's Kaliningrad exclave to the northeast, is a key logistics hub for delivering Western military aid to Ukraine and one of Kiev's main supporters in Europe. "GREAT NEWS! Thanks to the bold leadership of my friend, Karol Nawrocki, President of Poland, major progress is being made toward establishing a US Army base in Poland," Trump wrote on Truth Social on Thursday. "If this happens, the location will be announced very soon. This will be a historic step for our Great US/Polish Alliance," he added. Nawrocki responded by promising to find "the best possible location" for the base. "We are ready to continue our efforts to strengthen our defense cooperation: seriously, responsibly, and always together," he wrote on X. The US already maintains a permanent Army garrison and command headquarters in Poland, although most of the roughly 10,000 American troops stationed in the country serve on a rotational basis. During Trump's first term, Poland offered in 2018 to host a permanent base tentatively named "Fort Trump." Under Trump's successor, President Joe Biden, the US established a garrison headquartered at Camp Kosciuszko in Poznan and permanently stationed the V Corps Forward Headquarters in the city. Tensions between Russia and NATO have flared in recent months as eastern members of the US-led military bloc have blamed Russia for drone incursions. Moscow has dismissed the allegations as unfounded. Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski said during a trip to Kiev over the weekend that "if Russia attacked us and we took our gloves off, I think we would defeat Russia quite quickly." Russian presidential aide and former security chief Nikolay Patrushev responded to Sikorski by warning that "Polish statehood would cease to exist within two or three days" should a conflict break out. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov reiterated this week that the country had no intention of attacking NATO members, but said that if the bloc attacked Russia, the war would be "very short."
